title: Akiflow Fall Update: iCloud Calendar & Apple Watch
summary: Explore iCloud Calendar sync, Akiflow for Apple Watch, a redesigned desktop and Travel Time. Includes setup steps, requirements and FAQs.
body_markdown:
## Summary


-


At publication, Akiflow announced two-way iCloud Calendar event sync, requiring an Apple app-specific password and preserving read-only calendar permissions.


-


The announced Apple Watch companion could capture, browse, complete, and reopen tasks, while offline changes waited to sync through a paired iPhone.


-


The release also introduced a roomier desktop redesign and user-added Travel Time blocks, whose saved estimates did not automatically account for live traffic.


Your calendar shouldn’t make you choose between work and the rest of your life. And a task shouldn’t disappear just because you thought of it away from your desk.


Our fall update brings two much-requested additions to Akiflow: iCloud Calendar and an Apple Watch app. Alongside them, we’ve refreshed desktop and web and added Travel Time for in-person appointments. Together, these changes make it easier to capture a commitment, see where it fits, and leave enough time to get there.


## iCloud Calendar, right beside your tasks


If your personal calendar lives in iCloud, you can bring it into the same plan as your work. See an appointment alongside a project deadline, or make room for a family commitment before you fill the afternoon with tasks.


Akiflow’s iCloud Calendar integration supports two-way event sync. Create, edit, reschedule or delete an event in Akiflow, and the change syncs to iCloud. Changes in iCloud come back to Akiflow too. Calendar permissions still apply: a read-only calendar stays read-only.


Want a task to appear in iCloud Calendar? Use **Lock** to place it on a calendar you can edit. Simply scheduling the task inside Akiflow does not export it.


### How to connect iCloud Calendar


1.


Sign in to your[Apple Account](https://account.apple.com/) . Under Sign-In and Security, generate an app-specific password. Two-factor authentication must be enabled.


2.


In Akiflow, open **Settings > Calendars > Add calendar > iCloud Calendar** .


3.


Enter your Apple Account email and the app-specific password, connect, then return to Akiflow and allow time for the first sync.


This connects calendars stored in iCloud, not Apple Reminders, iCloud Mail or calendars stored only on your device. Sync runs periodically rather than instantly. The[iCloud Calendar setup guide](https://product.akiflow.com/en/help/articles/1050432-icloud-calendar) covers the details and troubleshooting.


## A task app for your Apple Watch


Remember something on your way out? Tap + on your Watch, dictate or type it, and get back to what you were doing. The task goes to your Akiflow Inbox so you can plan it later on your phone or computer.


You can browse your lists, complete or reopen tasks, and add an Akiflow complication to your watch face. It shows a current or upcoming task, event or Time Slot, so checking what’s next doesn’t have to mean opening your phone.


The Watch app is a companion, not a replacement for the planner. It requires **watchOS 10 or later and Akiflow 2.83 or later on a paired iPhone** . Captures made away from your iPhone are queued until the devices reconnect. Task text is saved as entered; dictating a date doesn’t schedule the task, and Aki isn’t available on the Watch.


Update Akiflow on your iPhone, then install it through the iPhone’s Watch app if it hasn’t appeared automatically. Open Akiflow on your iPhone once for the first sync. See the[Apple Watch guide](https://product.akiflow.com/help/articles/8121233-akiflow-for-apple-watch) for setup and supported actions.


## A cleaner desktop, with more room to plan


The desktop and web redesign puts Inbox, Today and Tasks at the top of the sidebar. You can pin up to five sections, projects or tags for faster access, and group your Inbox by source or project.


Search has its own redesigned page. Meet With and Share Availability move into the calendar header, freeing the space previously used by the right sidebar. Responsive and Dynamic calendar views help the schedule fit the space you have and the days ahead.


These are practical changes to the places you use repeatedly: finding a task, processing an Inbox and looking at the week. The first-open tour points out what’s moved. Our[release notes](https://product.akiflow.com/changelog/icloud-calendar-travel-time-akiflow-on-apple-watch-and-a) cover the rest of the redesign.


## Plan the journey, not just the meeting


A 2 p.m. appointment isn’t really a 2 p.m. commitment if it takes half an hour to get there. Add Travel Time from an event’s location controls and Akiflow places a block before it. Choose a driving, walking or cycling estimate, or enter your own duration.


The block moves with the event. Google Calendar and Outlook receive a separate busy event; iCloud uses the event’s native travel-time setting. With the relevant event reminders enabled, Akiflow can also notify you when it’s time to leave.


You add Travel Time yourself. Estimates don’t include live traffic or recalculate automatically, and the feature doesn’t move conflicting meetings. It works for timed events on editable calendars, not all-day events or locked tasks and Time Slots. Read the[Travel Time guide](https://product.akiflow.com/en/help/articles/9727858-travel-time) for provider-specific behavior.


## Try one change in your next day


Start with the part of your routine that needs it most: connect your personal iCloud calendar, capture a task from your wrist, or reserve the journey before your next appointment. Open the updated app to explore, or[download Akiflow for your device](https://akiflow.com/download) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What did the fall update announce for iCloud Calendar?


At publication, Akiflow said its iCloud Calendar integration supported two-way event sync. Users could create, edit, reschedule, or delete events in Akiflow and sync those changes to iCloud. The article distinguished events from tasks: scheduling a task in Akiflow did not export it, while Lock could place it on an editable calendar.


### How did the article say users should connect iCloud Calendar?


The published setup required an Apple Account with two-factor authentication and an app-specific password. In Akiflow, users were directed to Settings, Calendars, Add calendar, and iCloud Calendar, then to enter their Apple Account email and that password. The article noted that the first sync could take time and ran periodically rather than instantly.


### What could the Apple Watch companion do at publication time?


The announcement said users could capture tasks, browse lists, complete or reopen tasks, and add an Akiflow complication showing a current or upcoming task, event, or Time Slot. It described the Watch app as a companion rather than a planner replacement and said disconnected changes would sync after the Watch reconnected with its paired iPhone.


### What changed in the announced desktop and web redesign?


At publication, Akiflow said Inbox, Today, and Tasks moved to the top of the sidebar. Users could pin up to five sections, projects, or tags, group the Inbox, and use a redesigned search page. Meet With and Share Availability moved into the calendar header, while Responsive and Dynamic views helped the calendar fit available space.


### How did Travel Time work in this release?


The article said users could add a Travel Time block from an event’s location controls and choose a driving, walking, cycling, or custom duration. The block moved with the event, but users had to add it themselves. Estimates excluded live traffic, did not recalculate automatically, and did not move conflicting meetings.
